### what_to_do_first.details[1]
Sentence: Because the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and Finland lacks a unified pathway monitoring system, the team recommends reporting referral-to-treatment access times and flagging stalled handovers using THL guidance 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers.

Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers. | notes: the team's own DRAFT recommendation, not yet reviewed by mentors; not evidence. flags.sentence: All county treatment shares are crude—unadjusted for age or stage because stage at diagnosis is missing for ~48% of new patients—and treatment categories overlap, while Kuva 16 provides only digitised national age-adjusted curative reference lines of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women (±0.5 percentage points).
flags.problem: Missing stage (~48%) explains why shares cannot be stage-adjusted, not why they are unadjusted for age; also, Kuva 16 is a figure from which the national reference lines were digitised rather than Kuva 16 providing only national reference lines.

flags.problem: The cited roadmap claims specify 2029–2031 county adoption only for the coordinator guidance (q:abcbb06ae3), not for the national pathways (q:def306014c) or referral criteria (q:c61439b30f), which also specifically apply to five or at least the five most common cancers.
